brief: The Market Ear frames US equities as sitting at a technical inflection point, arguing oil is driving yields, yields are driving equities, and the next move in rates will decide which index breaks first. NDX is coiling inside a large triangle formation, holding its major rising trend line and back above its 100-day moving average. A break above the shorter-term falling trend line is the level to watch, and any breakout risks becoming aggressive. SPX remains range-bound in the pattern that has held since May, having just bounced off its 100-day moving average, with no medium-term trend established. Russell is testing a massive long-term trend line, with its 200-day moving average sitting slightly below current levels. Small caps have been punished by rising rates, and the note argues a pullback in yields could quickly bring buyers back. The note states markets are effectively all trading oil right now, since oil has driven rates and rates have driven equities, with Russell more affected by that chain than the other indices.
